item.title: Why study Diophantine equations?
item.description:
📝 Here's a sampling of some true equations in modular arithmetic: \[6 \equiv 2 \pmod{4},\] \[3 \equiv -3 \pmod{6},\] \[27 \equiv 0 \pmod{9}. Unique prime factorization has a consequence in modular arithmetic. \) In other words, the single modular arithmetic equation \[920 \equiv 2 \pmod{54}\] is equivalent to the two equations \[920 \equiv 2 \pmod{2},\] \[920 \equiv 2 \pmod{3^3}.
🔗 Read more: https://hidden-phenomena.com/articles/modular

item.title: The power of collaboration: How we can reduce traffic congestion
item.description:
📝 While individual vehicle routing is standard across all the top navigation products, optimizing routing system-wide is not yet present. During “treatment” days, the modified routing guided all trips that encountered the pre-selected congested segments toward alternative routes with similar travel times. These modifications reroute trips with similarly costing alternative paths away from these segments, thereby reducing the flow of traffic that would have otherwise been experienced within them.
🔗 Read more: https://research.google/blog/the-power-of-collaboration-how-we-can-reduce-traffic-congestion/
